definitionEn: To do something special to mark a happy day or event.
example: We celebrate the New Year with our whole family every year.

definitionEn: Something you give to someone, usually on a special occasion.
example: She bought a small gift for each child at the party.

definitionEn: A card with a message sent to wish someone well on a special day.
example: My grandmother sent me a colourful greeting card this morning.

definitionEn: A person invited to visit or attend an event at someone's home.
example: Every guest brought a small dish to share during dinner.

definitionEn: To ask someone politely to come to an event or your home.
example: We decided to invite all our neighbours to the picnic.

definitionEn: A short speech or gesture of raising a glass to honour someone.
example: Uncle Minh raised his glass for a warm toast to the couple.

definitionEn: A stick of wax with a wick that gives light when it is burned.
example: Dozens of candles glowed softly along the temple steps at night.

definitionEn: A sweet baked food, often made for a party or celebration.
example: The children waited eagerly for the big cake to be cut.

definitionEn: A small red envelope with money given as a gift at New Year.
example: Children happily received a red envelope from every elder in the family.

definitionEn: To wear your best or most formal clothes for a special occasion.
example: Many families dress up in bright new clothes for the spring festival.

definitionEn: Enjoyable, entertaining, or full of pleasure and laughter.
example: The street games were fun for kids and grandparents alike.

definitionEn: A large group of people gathered together in one place.
example: A huge crowd gathered along the river to watch the boat race.

definitionEn: Sounds made by instruments or voices arranged in patterns to be enjoyed.
example: Traditional music filled the courtyard as the sun went down.

definitionEn: The main meal of the day, often eaten in the evening.
example: After the ceremony, the whole village shared a long dinner together.

definitionEn: A raised platform where performers stand during a show or event.
example: Young dancers performed on a wooden stage beside the lake.

definitionEn: To make something look more attractive by adding colourful objects.
example: We decorate the house with red paper flowers before the New Year.

definitionEn: A meal eaten outdoors, usually taken to a park or open area.
example: We had a picnic in the park during the long holiday weekend.

definitionEn: A line of people waiting one behind another for their turn.
example: There was a long queue for the ferry to the island this morning.

definitionEn: A member of your family, such as a cousin, aunt or grandparent.
example: Many relatives travel back to their hometown every spring for the celebration.

definitionEn: To follow a custom, rule or tradition as it is expected.
example: Families observe the custom by cleaning their homes before the festival.

definitionEn: To be present at an event such as a ceremony, party or meeting.
example: Thousands of visitors attend the festival every year in early spring.

definitionEn: To take part in an activity or event together with other people.
example: Children are encouraged to participate in the traditional village games.

definitionEn: The place, time or source from which something first came or began.
example: Historians trace the origin of the festival back several centuries.

definitionEn: A god or goddess, especially one worshipped by a group of people.
example: Villagers pray to the local deity for a good harvest each year.

definitionEn: The gathering of crops when they are ripe, or the crops gathered.
example: The festival marks the end of the autumn harvest in many villages.

definitionEn: A very large quantity of something, more than enough.
example: The table overflowed with an abundance of fruit and sticky rice.

definitionEn: Decorated with many complicated details, patterns or carvings.
example: The temple gates were covered with ornate carvings of dragons and flowers.

definitionEn: Full of bright colour, energy and excitement.
example: The streets were filled with vibrant colours and joyful laughter.

definitionEn: Involving many carefully arranged parts or details.
example: The dancers wore elaborate costumes stitched with gold thread.

definitionEn: To feel or show great happiness, especially about a good event.
example: Families rejoice together when the spring festival finally begins.

definitionEn: To begin something, often used in formal or official contexts.
example: The lion dance will commence at noon in front of the pagoda.

definitionEn: A religious song of praise, sung by a group in worship.
example: The choir sang a gentle hymn as the candles were lit.

definitionEn: A raised table or structure used for offerings and prayers.
example: Fresh flowers and fruit were placed carefully on the family altar.

definitionEn: Sticks or powder that give off a sweet smell when burned.
example: The sweet smell of incense drifted through the quiet temple courtyard.

definitionEn: A musical instrument played by hitting its tight surface with hands or sticks.
example: The steady beat of a drum guided the dancers across the courtyard.

definitionEn: A large metal disc that makes a loud ringing sound when struck.
example: A deep gong announced the start of the traditional lion dance.

definitionEn: A traditional story that explains natural events or the beliefs of a people.
example: The myth tells how the first rice field was created by the gods.

definitionEn: Traditional stories, songs and customs passed down among ordinary people.
example: Many festival games are rooted in local folklore and old legends.

definitionEn: The date on which a special event happened in an earlier year.
example: The village held a grand festival to mark the anniversary of its founding.

definitionEn: Relating to the moon, especially to a calendar that follows its cycles.
example: The lunar calendar determines the date of many traditional festivals.

definitionEn: A member of your family who lived in the past, from whom you are descended.
example: Families honour their ancestors with food and incense on this day.

definitionEn: Something said or done to show respect and admiration for someone.
example: The poem was written as a tribute to the village elders.

definitionEn: To ask for divine favour or protection for a person or place.
example: The monk came to bless the new boats before the fishing season.

definitionEn: The part of a person that is not physical, or the feeling of a place or group.
example: The festival captures the spirit of unity that binds the community together.

definitionEn: A holy place dedicated to a god, saint or sacred person.
example: Pilgrims lit lamps at the small shrine on the hill each evening.

definitionEn: Showing signs that something good is likely to happen in the future.
example: Families chose an auspicious date for the opening of the festival.

definitionEn: To lift something up, usually by pulling on ropes or cords.
example: Volunteers hoist a red flag above the gate at dawn each day.

definitionEn: An event where people wear masks and costumes, or a deception disguised as something else.
example: The masquerade featured dancers wearing carved wooden masks and bright robes.

definitionEn: Noisy, lively celebration with music, dancing and enjoyment.
example: Revelry filled the streets long after the lanterns had been lit.

definitionEn: Cheerful laughter and enjoyment shared among a group of people.
example: Merriment echoed across the square as children chased paper kites.

definitionEn: A period of staying awake or gathering quietly, often at night, for a special purpose.
example: Villagers kept a quiet vigil by the river on the eve of the festival.

definitionEn: Honour or respect shown publicly towards a person, tradition or achievement.
example: The annual procession pays homage to the founders of the village.

definitionEn: The quality of being holy, sacred or deserving of deep respect.
example: Visitors are asked to respect the sanctity of the ancient temple grounds.

definitionEn: To feel deep respect and admiration for someone or something.
example: Elders are revered in the village for their wisdom and generosity.

definitionEn: Full of energy, enthusiasm and high spirits.
example: The exuberant crowd cheered every time the dragon dancers leapt forward.

definitionEn: A model or statue of a person, often used in a ritual or celebration.
example: A straw effigy was carried through the streets and then burned at dusk.

definitionEn: A holy place, or a safe and peaceful place where people can rest.
example: The old pagoda became a sanctuary for worshippers during the festival.

definitionEn: Relating to a formal ceremony or to an official ritual performed on special occasions.
example: The ceremonial opening began with the beating of ancient drums.

definitionEn: To express deep sorrow or regret, often publicly, about a loss.
example: Mourners lament the loss of the village chief in solemn songs.

definitionEn: A large, lively gathering or festival with entertainment for many people.
example: The three-day jamboree drew musicians from across the whole region.

definitionEn: The longest or shortest day of the year, when the sun is at its furthest point.
example: The winter solstice is marked by a candlelit feast in many cultures.

definitionEn: A colourful public show, often with costumes and parades, that tells a story.
example: The historical pageant retold the founding of the kingdom through song.

definitionEn: To produce echoing sound, or to have a lasting effect across a wide area.
example: The thunder of the drums reverberated across the valley all night.

definitionEn: A serious, formal and dignified quality, especially during a religious occasion.
example: The ceremony was conducted with great solemnity before the altar.

definitionEn: A formal prayer or call asking a god or spirit for help or blessing.
example: The priest began with an invocation to the spirits of the land.

definitionEn: Attractively bright, impressive and richly decorated.
example: The bride looked resplendent in her silk gown and gold jewellery.

definitionEn: A formal robe or garment worn by priests or officials during religious services.
example: The priest wore a white vestment embroidered with gold thread.

definitionEn: Something added to make a person or object look more attractive or decorative.
example: Silver adornments hung from the dancers' hair and sleeves during the performance.

definitionEn: Relating to a tribe, a traditional community bound by shared customs and ancestry.
example: The tribal dances tell stories of the ancestors who first settled here.

definitionEn: Bringing back memories of something similar from the past.
example: The music was reminiscent of the festivals of his childhood years.

definitionEn: To feel or protect something valuable with great care and affection.
example: Families cherish these festivals as a precious link to their roots.

definitionEn: To decorate something, or to add details that make a story more exciting.
example: Artisans embellish the wooden masks with paint and shining beads.

definitionEn: A person who protects, maintains or looks after something valuable.
example: Local elders serve as custodians of the festival's oldest traditions.

definitionEn: Deep respect and reverence given to a sacred person, object or relic.
example: Pilgrims show great veneration for the relics kept inside the shrine.

definitionEn: Deeply religious, or showing strong devotion to faith and holy duties.
example: Pious villagers walk barefoot to the temple on the first day.

definitionEn: Causing a feeling of excitement, energy and joy.
example: The fast boat race was an exhilarating finale to the three-day festival.

meaningVi: sôi nổi, tràn đầy sức sống
definitionEn: Lively, cheerful and full of bubbling enthusiasm.
example: The effervescent young performers filled the stage with laughter and song.

definitionEn: Cheerful, friendly and good-humoured in manner.
example: The jovial host greeted every visitor with a smile and a cup of tea.

definitionEn: Noisy, energetic and rowdy, especially in a happy and lively way.
example: A boisterous group of children ran through the market in bright costumes.

definitionEn: Impressive beauty, magnificence or richness of appearance.
example: The palace gardens showed their full splendour during the festival week.

definitionEn: To decorate something richly with many ornaments or colourful items.
example: The streets were bedecked with silk banners and glowing paper lamps.

definitionEn: Offered or given in fulfilment of a vow to a god or saint.
example: Worshippers placed votive candles before the statue as a sign of gratitude.

definitionEn: A blessing, or a short prayer asking for divine favour at the end of a service.
example: The elder pronounced a benediction over the gathered families at dusk.

definitionEn: The special clothes, ornaments and symbols of a ruler or a formal office.
example: The king's regalia, including a golden crown, was displayed for the festival.

definitionEn: Cheerful amusement, laughter or merriment expressed by a group.
example: Mirth rippled through the crowd as the clown performed his tricks.

definitionEn: To make a god or spirit favourable or calm through offerings or rituals.
example: Villagers offered rice and wine to propitiate the spirits of the river.

definitionEn: Regarded as holy, sacred and deserving great respect.
example: The hallowed grounds of the old temple are visited by thousands each year.

definitionEn: An offering given to a god, typically food or drink presented in worship.
example: Each family brought an oblation of fruit to the shrine at dawn.

definitionEn: A formal speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly.
example: The chief delivered a panegyric honouring the heroes of the village.

definitionEn: To declare something sacred, or dedicate it formally to a religious purpose.
example: The monks consecrated the new bell in a solemn ceremony at sunrise.

definitionEn: A feeling of intense joy, pride, or spiritual elevation.
example: The crowd erupted in exaltation when the dragon finally crossed the square.

definitionEn: To make something holy, or to give it religious approval and blessing.
example: The priest sprinkled water to sanctify the new fishing boats.

definitionEn: Regarded as so sacred or important that it must never be violated or changed.
example: For many families, the ancestral altar remains sacrosanct and carefully protected.

definitionEn: A sacred ritual, especially one considered a visible sign of divine grace.
example: The sacrament was performed quietly before the congregation at dawn.

definitionEn: The fixed forms of worship and ritual used in a religious service.
example: The temple liturgy has remained unchanged for many hundreds of years.

meaningVi: đỉnh cao, sự thần thánh hóa
definitionEn: The highest point of development, or elevation of a person to divine status.
example: The final dance was the apotheosis of the entire festival programme.

definitionEn: Having a strong spiritual quality that inspires awe and a feeling of the divine.
example: The misty mountain shrine felt numinous at dawn, hushed and sacred.

definitionEn: Relating to priests, or to a formal, traditional style used in sacred art.
example: The hieratic style of the murals reflects centuries of religious tradition.

definitionEn: A rousing song or hymn of praise, often associated with a nation or group.
example: The crowd joined in the festival anthem with great pride and emotion.

definitionEn: A covered litter carried on poles by people, used in the past to transport important figures.
example: The bride was carried to the ceremony in a richly decorated palanquin.

definitionEn: A short, loud sounding of trumpets to announce an important arrival or event.
example: A bright fanfare announced the arrival of the royal procession at noon.

definitionEn: Wild, drunken revelry, or a noisy celebration with excessive enjoyment.
example: The harvest party turned into a bacchanalia of music, wine and dancing.

definitionEn: Lighthearted joy and a cheerful, happy mood.
example: The gaiety of the spring festival was felt in every home and street.

definitionEn: Lively energy, enthusiasm and high spirits shown openly by a person or group.
example: The children showed great exuberance as they chased the lion dancers.

definitionEn: Great happiness and triumph, often expressed loudly by a group of people.
example: Jubilation spread across the village when the rains finally arrived.

definitionEn: A brilliant radiance or splendour, especially of light or sunshine.
example: The lanterns shone with a warm effulgence over the sleeping village.

definitionEn: The images, symbols and motifs used in religious or cultural art and tradition.
example: The iconography of the festival mask reveals its ancient spiritual meaning.

definitionEn: A priest or leader who interprets sacred mysteries and rituals to others.
example: The hierophant led the procession wearing a robe covered in sacred symbols.

definitionEn: A splendid or impressive display, often of ceremonial clothes or equipment.
example: The troops marched in full panoply, their banners gleaming in the sunlight.

definitionEn: Relating to sacred rites or religious worship, rather than to ordinary life.
example: Sacral music echoed through the stone halls during the midnight service.

definitionEn: To decorate something by hanging garlands, ribbons or flowers across it.
example: Villagers festoon the gateway with ribbons and flowers before the parade.

definitionEn: Covered with a thin layer of gold, or looking luxurious and splendid.
example: The gilded statues of the Buddha glittered in the light of the candles.

meaningVi: sự dồi dào, cảnh sung túc
definitionEn: A large abundance of good things, or a symbol of plenty filled with fruit.
example: The harvest table was a cornucopia of rice, fruit, vegetables and sweets.

definitionEn: A slow, mournful song or piece of music sung or played for the dead.
example: A solemn dirge was sung at the riverside as the boats drifted away.

definitionEn: Relating to marriage or to the ceremony and rituals of a wedding.
example: The nuptial procession wound through the village lanes under lanterns.

definitionEn: A person, especially a monk, who lives by begging for food and alms.
example: A mendicant monk walked barefoot from village to village at dawn.

definitionEn: A visible appearance or manifestation of a god to a person or community.
example: Villagers described the sudden storm as a theophany that blessed the crops.

definitionEn: A state of intense joy or delight that seems to lift a person out of themselves.
example: The dancers swayed in rapture as the drums grew louder and faster.

definitionEn: Cheerful, lively enthusiasm and a sense of exuberant high spirits.
example: The host's ebullience made every guest feel welcome at the festival feast.

definitionEn: A state of pleasant daydreaming or being lost in thoughts of the past.
example: She drifted into reverie, remembering the lanterns of her childhood festivals.
